fixes.explanation: Oh, I wish it worked that way, friend, but that's not what the verse says. God says, "Will not your creditors suddenly arise and those who disturb you awaken? Then you will become their prey." (Habakkuk 2:7). The verse has them waking up and rising suddenly, and he becomes their prey. I bet they brought their receipts.

That's right, baker. God says, "Woe to him who builds a city with bloodshed and establishes a town by iniquity!" (Habakkuk 2:12). That's woe number three in this passage. The woe before it was about a house in verse 9. This one is about a whole city built with bloodshed.

Right, baker. "For its maker trusts in his own creation; he makes idols that cannot speak." (Habakkuk 2:18). The maker trusts what he made, and what he made can't say a single word back. The verse even calls the idol a teacher of lies.
